messages:
omar: Heads up — after the 11:28 deploy I'm seeing large client LCP spikes and sparklines freeze on first interaction in EU canary. Charts are mostly fine after first paint but first interaction blocks ~300-700ms.

katie: Which routes/metrics? link to dashboard? @marta can you take a look? :eyes:

omar: Telemetry snippet:
```
kvcache.miss_rate{env:prod,region:eu,route:console} = 0.47
console.client.lcp.p50{canary=true,region=eu} jumped from 230ms -> 720ms after deploy
trace sample: /console/widgets/sparkline -> main_thread_block: 420ms; js_parse: 120ms; event_loop: queuing spikes
```

marta: I ran a quick bundle diff on the canary build — charting bundle gzipped increased by ~115KB. There's a new chunk boundary for intl + date-utils that used to be in the app chunk. Also noticed prefetch TTL for priority group was changed in the rollout PR earlier today.

sam: That TTL change was from PR #8345 (author: eng-prefetch). The change set includes: `prefetch.groups.priority.defaultTTL = 0s` (was 30s). commit 9f3a2d6

omar: If TTL=0 then prefetch never caches across navigations -> repeated kvcache cold starts. Makes sense with the miss_rate spike.

katie: Can we revert TTL change in canary quickly? Which is lower risk — revert TTL or rollback the whole deploy?

marta: Reverting TTL in config is low-risk and should give immediate relief. But bundle bump and new chunk boundary still need follow-up — that explains parse cpu increase. I recommend revert TTL on canary now and queue a small rollback if we see no improvement.

sam: Agreed. Also adding a quick patch to pin kvcache affinity key to route+user so cold prefetches are less likely to blow up traffic. Patch in flight: #8352.

omar: Running quick telemetry after config flip...

deploybot: deploybot: Applied config override to canary: prefetch.priority.defaultTTL=30s at 4176543450

omar: New telemetry (2m after change):
```
kvcache.miss_rate{env:prod,region:eu,route:console} = 0.06
console.client.lcp.p50{canary=true,region=eu} = 250ms
trace sample: main_thread_block reduced to ~40-60ms
```

katie: Nice. Confirmed metrics look back to baseline. Great call. 

marta: I'll open a perf issue for the bundle chunking regression and link the PR that introduced the change. We should add a CI perf check that fails if gzipped charting bundle > baseline + 50KB.

sam: I'll land the kvcache affinity pin (non-breaking) and add unit tests. Follow-ups: #8353 (bundle audit), #8354 (perf CI).

omar: For the postmortem: root cause = prefetch config change + unexpected chunk boundary that increased parse time, combined led to high kvcache misses and first-interaction stalls. Fix path = revert TTL + backfill chunking audit and perf tests.

katie: Assigning to eng-platform perf board. Can someone add a short runbook step to detect similar regressions earlier? e.g., alert when kvcache.miss_rate increase > 10% over baseline in any region.

marta: Adding runbook note and perf harness snapshot now.

sam: Opening the GH issues and tagging ops/sre.

omar: Thanks everyone. Marking canary stabilized. :white_check_mark:

katie: :thumbsup:
